questions.text: Ca²⁺ और Cl⁻ आयनों की मोलर आयनिक चालकताएँ क्रमश: 119.0 और 76.3 S cm² mol⁻¹ हैं। CaCl₂ के लिए सीमांत मोलर चालकता का मान होगा:
questions.text_english: The molar ionic conductivities of Ca²⁺ and Cl⁻ are 119.0 and 76.3 S cm² mol⁻¹ respectively. The value of limiting molar conductivity of CaCl₂ will be:
questions.solution: For CaCl₂, the formula for limiting molar conductivity is: Λ°m(CaCl₂) = Λ°(Ca²⁺) + 2 × Λ°(Cl⁻). Since CaCl₂ dissociates to give one Ca²⁺ and two Cl⁻ ions, we must multiply the chloride conductivity by 2. Therefore, Λ°m = 119.0 + 2 × 76.3 = 119.0 + 152.6 = 271.6 S cm² mol⁻¹. Option D is correct. Options A and C are wrong because they do not account correctly for two Cl⁻ ions; option B is simply the difference of the two values.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया पर विचार कीजिए: HCHO + HCHO + सांद्र KOH → A + B। दिए गए विकल्पों में से A और B की पहचान कीजिए:
questions.text_english: Consider the following reaction: HCHO + HCHO + Conc. KOH → A + B. Identify A and B from the given options:
questions.solution: This reaction is the Cannizzaro reaction, which occurs when an aldehyde without an alpha-hydrogen is treated with concentrated alkali. Formaldehyde (HCHO) has no alpha-hydrogen. In this disproportionation, one molecule of HCHO is oxidised to potassium formate (HCOOK) and the other is reduced to methanol (CH₃OH). Hence A is Methanol and B is Potassium formate, which is option A. Ethanol and potassium acetate arise from acetaldehyde, not formaldehyde.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित अम्लों में से कौन विटामिन C को निरूपित करता है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following acids represents Vitamin C?
questions.solution: Vitamin C is chemically known as Ascorbic acid (option C). It is a water-soluble vitamin essential for collagen synthesis and acts as an antioxidant. Saccharic acid is an oxidation product of glucose, gluconic acid is produced by mild oxidation of glucose at the aldehyde end, and benzoic acid is a simple aromatic carboxylic acid — none of these represent Vitamin C.

questions.text: ऐल्डिहाइडों के विरचन के लिए रोज़ेनमुण्ड अपचयन प्रयुक्त होता है। इस अभिक्रिया में प्रयुक्त उत्प्रेरक है:
questions.text_english: Rosenmund reduction is used for the preparation of Aldehydes. The catalyst used in this reaction is:
questions.solution: In the Rosenmund reduction, an acid chloride (RCOCl) is selectively reduced to an aldehyde (RCHO) by passing hydrogen gas over palladium poisoned with barium sulphate (Pd–BaSO₄), which is option A. BaSO₄ acts as a poison to partially deactivate Pd, preventing the further reduction of the aldehyde to an alcohol. Anhydrous AlCl₃ is used in Friedel–Crafts reactions, Iron (III) oxide in industrial synthesis, and HgSO₄ in the hydration of alkynes.

questions.text: दिए गए विकल्पों में से कौन सा ऐल्किल हैलाइड Sₙ1 अभिक्रिया अधिक तीव्रता से करेगा?
questions.text_english: Which alkyl halide from the given options will undergo Sₙ1 reaction faster?
questions.solution: The Sₙ1 reaction proceeds through the formation of a carbocation intermediate; thus its rate depends on the stability of the carbocation formed. (CH₃)₃C–Br is a tertiary alkyl halide that forms a tertiary carbocation upon ionisation, which is the most stable due to hyperconjugation and inductive effect of three methyl groups. Hence option A undergoes Sₙ1 fastest. Option B (secondary) and C (primary) form less stable carbocations, and option D is a neopentyl halide (primary, sterically hindered) which reacts very slowly by Sₙ1.

questions.text: नीचे दिए हुए 3d श्रेणी के तत्वों में से कौन सर्वाधिक संख्या में ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाएँ दर्शाता है?
questions.text_english: From the elements of 3d series given below, which element shows the maximum number of oxidation states?
questions.solution: Manganese (Mn, Z = 25) shows the maximum number of oxidation states among the 3d series elements. Its electronic configuration is [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s², and it exhibits oxidation states from +2 to +7 (i.e., +2, +3, +4, +5, +6, +7), giving it the widest range. Chromium shows +2 to +6, titanium shows +2 to +4, and scandium mainly shows only +3. Therefore option B is correct.

questions.text: आरेनिअस समीकरण का सही गणितीय व्यंजक है:
questions.text_english: The correct Mathematical expression of Arrhenius equation is:
questions.solution: The Arrhenius equation relates the rate constant k to the activation energy Ea and temperature T. The correct expression is k = Ae^(–Ea/RT), where A is the pre-exponential (frequency) factor, R is the gas constant, and T is the absolute temperature (option C). The negative sign in the exponent indicates that the rate constant decreases as activation energy increases. Options A and D are incorrect because k cannot be negative; option B omits the frequency factor A and has the wrong sign.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से तृतीयक ऐमीन की पहचान कीजिए:
questions.text_english: Identify the tertiary amine from the following:
questions.solution: A tertiary amine has the nitrogen atom bonded to three carbon-containing groups with no N–H bond. In option A, the nitrogen is bonded to three methyl groups (trimethylamine), making it a tertiary amine. Option B has an –NH₂ group attached to a secondary carbon, making it a primary amine. Option C has nitrogen bonded to two carbon groups with one N–H bond, so it is a secondary amine. Option D also has –NH₂ making it primary. Hence option A is correct.

questions.text: कीटोनों में ग्रीन्यार अभिकर्मक की योगज अभिक्रिया के पश्चात तनु अम्लों द्वारा जलअपघटन से निर्मित होता है:
questions.text_english: Nucleophilic addition of Grignard reagent to ketones followed by hydrolysis with dilute acids forms:
questions.solution: When a Grignard reagent (RMgX) adds to a ketone (R’COR’’), the Grignard reagent's carbanion attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon. After hydrolysis with dilute acid, the product is a tertiary alcohol because the carbon now bears three carbon substituents (two from the ketone and one from the Grignard reagent) and an –OH group. When Grignard reagent reacts with formaldehyde it gives primary alcohol, with other aldehydes it gives secondary alcohol, but with ketones it always gives tertiary alcohol. Hence option C is correct.

questions.text: शून्य कोटि की अभिक्रिया के लिए दिए गए ग्राफ में ढाल और अंत:खंड हैं:
questions.text_english: In a given graph of zero order reaction, the slope and intercept are:
questions.solution: For a zero order reaction, the integrated rate equation is [R] = [R]₀ – kt. When concentration [R] is plotted against time t, the graph is a straight line. Comparing with y = mx + c, the slope is –k (negative because concentration decreases with time) and the y-intercept is [R]₀ (the initial concentration). Hence option B is correct. Options C and D correspond to first order reactions where ln[R] is plotted against time.

दी हुई अभिक्रियाओं के लिए अभिकर्मकों के साथ सुमेलित कीजिए:
I. प्राथमिक एल्कोहॉलों का एल्डिहाइडों में ऑक्सीकरण – (p) NaBH₄
II. ब्यूटेन-2-ओन से ब्यूटेन-2-ऑल – (q) 440 K पर 85% फॉस्फोरिक अम्ल
III. फीनॉल का 2, 4, 6-ट्राइब्रोमोफीनॉल में ब्रोमीनन – (r) PCC
IV. प्रोपेन-2-ऑल का प्रोपीन में निर्जलीकरण – (s) ब्रोमीन जल
questions.text_english:
Match the reagents required for the given reactions:
I. Oxidation of primary alcohols to aldehydes – (p) NaBH₄
II. Butan-2-one to Butan-2-ol – (q) 85% phosphoric acid at 440 K
III. Bromination of Phenol to 2, 4, 6-Tribromophenol – (r) PCC
IV. Dehydration of propan-2-ol to propene – (s) Bromine water
questions.solution: PCC (Pyridinium chlorochromate) selectively oxidises primary alcohols to aldehydes without over-oxidising to carboxylic acids, so I matches with (r). NaBH₄ is a mild reducing agent that reduces ketones like butan-2-one to the corresponding secondary alcohol butan-2-ol, so II matches with (p). Bromine water reacts directly with phenol by electrophilic aromatic substitution at ortho and para positions to give 2,4,6-tribromophenol, so III matches with (s). 85% phosphoric acid at 440 K is used for dehydration of alcohols to alkenes, so IV matches with (q). Hence option A is correct.

questions.text: d-ब्लॉक तत्वों का सामान्य इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास है:
questions.text_english: The general electronic configuration of d-block elements is:
questions.solution: d-block elements have their differentiating electron entering the (n–1)d orbitals. The general electronic configuration is (n–1) d¹⁻¹⁰ ns¹⁻², where the d orbitals can accommodate 1 to 10 electrons and the s orbital can have 1 or 2 electrons. This is option A. Option B specifies only d¹⁰ which does not capture the range. Option C has an incorrect s orbital range (2–3 is not possible). Option D with d⁰ would represent s-block or p-block elements, not d-block.

sub_questions.text_english: Order of a reaction

sub_questions.solution: The order of a reaction is defined as the sum of the powers (exponents) of the concentration terms of the reactants present in the experimentally determined rate law expression. For a reaction with rate = k[A]^m[B]^n, the overall order is (m + n). It may be zero, a positive integer, or even a fraction.

sub_questions.solution: Activation energy (Ea) is defined as the minimum extra amount of energy that the reactant molecules must possess over their average energy in order to collide effectively and form the activated complex (transition state). It is the energy barrier that must be overcome for a reaction to occur. Higher activation energy means a slower reaction at a given temperature.

questions.text: 200 g जल में किसी अवाष्पशील विलेय के 18 g घोलकर बना विलयन 272.07 K पर हिमभूत होता है। विलेय का आण्विक द्रव्यमान परिकलित कीजिए। (जल के लिए Kₑ = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹)
questions.text_english: 18 g of a non-volatile solute is dissolved in 200 g of H₂O freezes at 272.07 K. Calculate the molecular mass of solute (Kₑ for water = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹)

key_points: Delta Tf = 273.15 - 272.07 = 1.08 K (depression in freezing point)
Molality m = Delta Tf / Kf = 1.08/1.86 = 0.5806 mol/kg
Moles of solute = 0.5806 x 0.2 = 0.11612 mol
Molecular mass = 18/0.11612 = 155.0 g/mol

questions.solution: The freezing point of pure water is 273.15 K. The solution freezes at 272.07 K, so the depression in freezing point ΔT = 273.15 – 272.07 = 1.08 K. Using the formula ΔT = K × m, where m is the molality: m = ΔT / K = 1.08 / 1.86 = 0.5806 mol kg⁻¹. The mass of solvent is 200 g = 0.2 kg. Moles of solute = 0.5806 × 0.2 = 0.11613 mol. Molecular mass = mass / moles = 18 / 0.11613 ≈ 155 g mol⁻¹.

sub_questions.text_english: Which compound in the given pair would undergo Sₙ 2 reaction at a faster rate and why? CH₃–CH₂–I and CH₃–CH₂–Br

key_points: CH3-CH2-I undergoes SN2 faster
C-I bond is longer and weaker than C-Br bond
Iodide is a better leaving group

sub_questions.solution: CH₃–CH₂–I (iodoethane) undergoes Sₙ2 reaction faster. In Sₙ2 reactions, the rate depends on the ease of breaking the C–X bond. The C–I bond is longer and weaker than the C–Br bond, so it is more easily broken. Additionally, iodide (I⁻) is a better leaving group because it is a larger, more polarisable ion and its conjugate acid HI is a strong acid. Hence iodoethane reacts faster by Sₙ2 mechanism.

sub_questions.text_english: Write the stepwise mechanism of nucleophilic addition reactions in the carbonyl compounds.

key_points: Step 1: Nucleophile attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon
Step 2: Pi bond breaks, electrons shift to oxygen forming alkoxide intermediate
Step 3: Protonation of alkoxide by acid or water to give product

sub_questions.solution: The nucleophilic addition to carbonyl compounds occurs in two steps. In step 1, the nucleophile (Nu⁻) attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon from above or below the plane, breaking the C=O pi bond. The electrons of the pi bond shift to the oxygen atom, forming a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate with a negative charge on oxygen. In step 2, the alkoxide intermediate gets protonated by a proton source (water or acid) to give the final addition product (an alcohol). For example, when HCN adds to formaldehyde, CN⁻ attacks the carbonyl carbon to give an alkoxide, which is then protonated to give glycolonitrile (HOCH₂CN).

sub_questions.text_english: Toluene to benzoic acid

The methyl group is oxidised to -COOH group

sub_questions.solution: Toluene (C₆H₅CH₃) is converted to benzoic acid (C₆H₅COOH) by vigorous oxidation of the methyl group using acidic potassium permanganate (KMnO₄/H⁺) or alkaline KMnO₄ followed by acidification. The side chain –CH₃ is oxidised to the carboxyl group –COOH regardless of the length of the alkyl chain, giving benzoic acid.

Two molecules of ethanal undergo aldol condensation in dilute NaOH

sub_questions.solution: Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) is first oxidised to ethanal (CH₃CHO) using a mild oxidising agent such as PCC or acidic K₂Cr₂O₇. Then, two molecules of ethanal undergo aldol condensation in the presence of dilute NaOH. In this reaction, the alpha-hydrogen of one molecule of ethanal is removed to form a carbanion which attacks the carbonyl carbon of the second molecule of ethanal, giving 3-hydroxybutanal (CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CHO).

sub_questions.solution: In [Pt(en)₂Cl₂]²⁺, 'en' (ethylenediamine) is a bidentate ligand that can only occupy adjacent (cis) positions due to its short chain. The complex is square planar. Two geometrical isomers exist: (1) Cis isomer, in which the two Cl⁻ ligands are on the same side of the complex (adjacent positions), and the two 'en' groups are also adjacent; (2) Trans isomer, in which the two Cl⁻ ligands are on opposite sides of the square plane. sub_questions.solution: When Δ₀ < P (crystal field splitting energy is less than pairing energy), the complex is a high spin (outer orbital) complex. In this case, electrons prefer to occupy the higher energy e orbitals rather than pairing up in the lower t₂ orbitals. For a d⁴ ion in an octahedral field with weak field ligands (Δ₀ < P), one electron goes into each of the three t₂ orbitals and the fourth electron goes to the e orbital. The electronic configuration is t₂³ e¹.

sub_questions.solution: A unidentate ligand is one that has only one donor atom and therefore forms only one coordinate (dative) bond with the central metal atom or ion. In other words, it can donate one lone pair of electrons to the central metal at a time. Examples of unidentate ligands include ammonia (NH₃), water (H₂O), chloride ion (Cl⁻), cyanide ion (CN⁻), and carbon monoxide (CO).

Sn/Sn²⁺ (0.001M) ‖ H⁺ (0.01 M) | H₂(g)(1 bar)/Pt(s)
दिया है: E°(Sn²⁺/Sn) = –0.14 V, E° H⁺/H₂ = 0.00 V (log 10 = 1)
questions.text_english:
Calculate emf of the following cell at 25 °C:
Sn/Sn²⁺ (0.001M) ‖ H⁺ (0.01 M) | H₂(g)(1 bar) | Pt(s)
Given: E°(Sn²⁺/Sn) = –0.14 V, E° H⁺/H₂ = 0.00 V (log 10 = 1)

key_points: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = 0.00 - (-0.14) = 0.14 V
Apply Nernst equation: E = E° - (0.0591/n) log Q

questions.solution: The cell reaction is: Sn → Sn²⁺ + 2e⁻ (anode) and 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂ (cathode). E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = 0.00 – (–0.14) = +0.14 V. Using the Nernst equation at 25°C: E = E° – (0.0591/n) × log Q. The reaction quotient Q = [Sn²⁺] / [H⁺]² = 0.001 / (0.01)² = 0.001 / 0.0001 = 10. Number of electrons transferred n = 2. Therefore, E = 0.14 – (0.0591/2) × log 10 = 0.14 – 0.02955 × 1 = 0.14 – 0.02955 ≈ 0.1105 V. The EMF of the cell at 25°C is approximately 0.11 V.

sub_questions.text: हाइड्रोबोरॉनन–ऑक्सीकरण अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: Hydroboration–oxidation reaction

key_points: Alkene reacts with diborane to give trialkylborane
Trialkylborane is oxidised with H2O2/NaOH to give anti-Markovnikov alcohol

sub_questions.solution: In the hydroboration–oxidation reaction, an alkene (e.g., propene CH₃CH=CH₂) reacts with diborane (B₂H₆) to form a trialkylborane. The boron adds to the less substituted carbon (anti-Markovnikov addition). The trialkylborane is then oxidised with alkaline hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂/NaOH) to give the corresponding primary alcohol with anti-Markovnikov regioselectivity. For propene: CH₃CH=CH₂ + B₂H₆ → (CH₃CH₂CH₂)₃B → H₂O₂/NaOH → CH₃CH₂CH₂OH (propan-1-ol). The overall addition of water is anti-Markovnikov and syn.

sub_questions.text: विलियम्सन संश्लेषण
sub_questions.text_english: Williamson Synthesis

key_points: Sodium alkoxide reacts with alkyl halide by SN2 mechanism
Product is ether

sub_questions.solution: Williamson synthesis is an SN2 reaction used to prepare ethers. In this reaction, sodium alkoxide (RO⁻Na⁺) reacts with a primary alkyl halide (R’X) to form an ether (R–O–R’). For example: C₂H₅ONa + C₂H₅Br → C₂H₅–O–C₂H₅ + NaBr (diethyl ether). The alkoxide ion acts as a nucleophile and displaces the halide ion from the primary alkyl halide. Secondary or tertiary alkyl halides give elimination products instead, so primary halides must be used.

sub_questions.text: ऐनिसोल का फ्रीडेल–क्राफ्ट्स ऐल्किलन
sub_questions.text_english: Friedel-Crafts Alkylation of Anisole

key_points: Anisole reacts with alkyl halide in presence of anhydrous AlCl3
Methoxy group is ortho/para directing, so alkyl group goes to ortho and para positions

sub_questions.solution: In the Friedel–Crafts alkylation of anisole, anisole (C₆H₅OCH₃) reacts with an alkyl halide (e.g., CH₃Cl) in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃ as Lewis acid catalyst. The –OCH₃ group is an electron-donating, ortho/para-directing group, so the alkyl group preferentially enters the ortho and para positions of the ring. The equation is: C₆H₅OCH₃ + CH₃Cl —AlCl₃→ o-CH₃C₆H₄OCH₃ + p-CH₃C₆H₄OCH₃ + HCl. The major products are 2-methoxytoluene (ortho) and 4-methoxytoluene (para).

sub_questions.text: राइमर–टीमन अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: Reimer-Tiemann Reaction

key_points: Phenol reacts with CHCl3 and NaOH to give salicylaldehyde
The CHO group is introduced at the ortho position

sub_questions.solution: In the Reimer–Tiemann reaction, phenol is treated with chloroform (CHCl₃) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH) to introduce a formyl (–CHO) group at the ortho position of the phenol ring. The intermediate dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂) is generated from CHCl₃ and NaOH, which reacts with the phenoxide ring. After hydrolysis, salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) is formed. The equation is: C₆H₅OH + CHCl₃ + 3NaOH → 2-HOC₆H₄CHO (salicylaldehyde) + 3NaCl + 2H₂O.

sub_questions.text: फीनॉल और बेन्जोइक अम्ल में विभेद
sub_questions.text_english: Chemical test to distinguish Phenol and Benzoic acid

key_points: FeCl3 test: Phenol gives violet/purple colour; benzoic acid gives buff precipitate
NaHCO3 test: Benzoic acid gives brisk effervescence of CO2; phenol does not

sub_questions.solution: Test 1 – Ferric chloride test: Add a few drops of neutral FeCl₃ solution to each compound dissolved in water. Phenol gives a characteristic violet or purple colour due to formation of a phenol–iron complex. Benzoic acid gives a buff-coloured precipitate of ferric benzoate. Test 2 – NaHCO₃ test: Add sodium bicarbonate solution to each compound. Benzoic acid dissolves with brisk effervescence (CO₂ gas is evolved) because it is a stronger acid than carbonic acid. Phenol does not produce effervescence with NaHCO₃ as it is a weaker acid than carbonic acid.

sub_questions.text: प्रोपेनेल और प्रोपेनोन में विभेद
sub_questions.text_english: Chemical test to distinguish Propanal and Propanone

key_points: Tollens' test: Propanal gives silver mirror; propanone does not
Fehling's test: Propanal gives brick-red precipitate; propanone does not

sub_questions.solution: Tollens' reagent test: Add Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) to each compound and warm gently. Propanal (an aldehyde) reduces Tollens' reagent and deposits a shiny silver mirror on the walls of the test tube. Propanone (a ketone) does not react with Tollens' reagent. Fehling's test can also be used: propanal gives a brick-red precipitate of Cu₂O upon warming with Fehling's solution, whereas propanone gives no change.

sub_questions.text: दिए हुए यौगिकों में से कौन प्रबलतर अम्ल है और क्यों? CH₂FCH₂CH₂COOH या CH₃CHFCH₂COOH
sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the given compounds is a stronger acid and why? CH₂FCH₂CH₂COOH or CH₃CHFCH₂COOH

key_points: CH2FCH2CH2COOH is stronger acid
F is closer to COOH in the other compound so more inductive stabilisation but F is farther from COOH in CH2FCH2CH2COOH
Actually CH3CHFCH2COOH has F closer to COOH group, so it is the stronger acid

sub_questions.solution: CH₃CHFCH₂COOH is the stronger acid. The electron-withdrawing fluorine atom stabilises the carboxylate anion (conjugate base) through the inductive effect. The closer the electronegative substituent is to the –COOH group, the stronger the inductive effect and hence the greater the acid strength. In CH₃CHFCH₂COOH, the F atom is on the carbon adjacent to the –CH₂COOH, i.e., at the β-carbon (2 carbons from COOH), while in CH₂FCH₂CH₂COOH, the F is at the γ-carbon (3 carbons from COOH). Since F is closer to the –COOH group in CH₃CHFCH₂COOH, it exerts a stronger electron-withdrawing inductive effect, better stabilising the carboxylate anion. Therefore CH₃CHFCH₂COOH is the stronger acid.

sub_questions.text_english: Essential amino acids

key_points: Amino acids that cannot be synthesised by the body and must be obtained from diet

sub_questions.solution: Essential amino acids are those amino acids that cannot be synthesised by the human body in adequate amounts and therefore must be obtained from dietary sources. There are nine essential amino acids: histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, and valine. Their deficiency leads to various metabolic disorders and diseases.

sub_questions.text: पेप्टाइड बंध
sub_questions.text_english: Peptide bond

key_points: Amide bond formed between -COOH group of one amino acid and -NH2 group of another amino acid with loss of water

sub_questions.solution: A peptide bond is a covalent amide bond formed between the carboxyl group (–COOH) of one amino acid and the amino group (–NH₂) of another amino acid, with the elimination of a water molecule. The resulting linkage is –CO–NH–, called the peptide linkage. Two amino acids joined by one peptide bond form a dipeptide; many amino acids joined by multiple peptide bonds form a polypeptide or protein.

sub_questions.text: विकृतीकरण
sub_questions.text_english: Denaturation

key_points: Disruption of secondary and tertiary structure of protein by physical or chemical means
Biological activity is lost but primary structure remains intact

sub_questions.solution: Denaturation is the process by which a protein loses its secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structure (native conformation) due to physical agents (heat, UV radiation) or chemical agents (acids, bases, heavy metal salts, organic solvents), while the primary structure (sequence of amino acids) remains intact. The protein loses its biological activity upon denaturation. A common example is the coagulation of egg white (albumin) on boiling.

sub_questions.text_english: The presence of -NO2 group at ortho or para position increases the reactivity of haloarenes towards nucleophilic substitution reactions. Give reason.

key_points: -NO2 is electron withdrawing and withdraws electron density from the ring through resonance
This makes the carbon bearing the halogen more electrophilic
Nucleophilic attack is facilitated

sub_questions.solution: The nitro group (–NO₂) is a powerful electron-withdrawing group. When present at the ortho or para position relative to the halogen, it withdraws electron density from the aromatic ring through resonance (mesomeric effect), particularly from the carbon bearing the halogen. This makes that carbon more electron-deficient (more electrophilic), facilitating the attack by a nucleophile. The Meisenheimer complex intermediate formed during the reaction is also stabilised by the –NO₂ group through resonance. Thus, the rate of nucleophilic aromatic substitution increases with –NO₂ at ortho/para positions.

Ethylene (ethene) is formed along with KCl and water

sub_questions.solution: When ethyl chloride (C₂H₅Cl) is treated with alcoholic potassium hydroxide (KOH in ethanol), a dehydrohalogenation (elimination, E2) reaction occurs. The alcoholic KOH acts as a strong base and abstracts a beta-hydrogen from the ethyl chloride, while the Cl⁻ leaves simultaneously. The product is ethene (CH₂=CH₂) along with potassium chloride and water. The equation is: CH₃–CH₂–Cl + KOH (alc.) → CH₂=CH₂ + KCl + H₂O. Aqueous KOH would give substitution (alcohol) instead.

questions.text: दर्शाइए कि प्रथम कोटि की अभिक्रिया में 99.9% अभिक्रिया पूर्ण होने में लगा समय अभिक्रिया की अर्धायु (t½) का 10 गुना होता है। [log 2 = 0.3010, log 10 = 1].
questions.text_english: Show that the time required for 99.9% completion in a first order reaction is 10 times of half-life (t½) of the reaction [log 2 = 0.3010, log 10 = 1].
questions.solution: For a first order reaction, the integrated rate equation gives: t = (2.303/k) × log([R]₀/[R]). For 99.9% completion, 99.9% of the reactant has reacted and only 0.1% remains. So [R] = 0.1% of [R]₀ = 0.001[R]₀. Therefore, t₉₉.₉% = (2.303/k) × log(100/0.1) = (2.303/k) × log(1000) = (2.303/k) × 3. The half-life of a first order reaction is t½ = 0.693/k = (2.303 × 0.3010)/k. The ratio t₉₉.₉% / t½ = [(2.303 × 3)/k] / [(2.303 × 0.3010)/k] = 3/0.3010 ≈ 9.97 ≈ 10. Hence, the time required for 99.9% completion is approximately 10 times the half-life of the first order reaction.

questions.text: उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों में आबंधन की प्रकृति, संरचना की व्याख्या संयोजकता आबंध सिद्धांत द्वारा कुछ हद तक की जा सकती है। केंद्रीय धातु परमाणु/आयन उपसहसंयोजन संख्या के बराबर रिक्त कक्षक उपलब्ध कराते हैं। धातु के उपयुक्त परमाण्विक कक्षक (s, p और d) संकरित करके निश्चित ज्यामितियों जैसे वर्ग समतली, चतुष्फलकीय एवं अष्ट-फलकीय आदि के समकक्ष कक्षकों के समुच्चय देते हैं। एक प्रबल सहसंयोजक आबंध तभी बनता है जब कक्षक अधिकतम अतिव्यापन करते हैं। संकरण में सम्मिलित d-कक्षक या तो आंतरिक d-कक्षक यानि (n-1) d अथवा बाह्य d-कक्षक यानि nd हो सकते हैं। इस प्रकार निर्मित संकुल क्रमश: आंतरिक कक्षक संकुल (निम्न प्रचक्रण संकुल) और बाह्य कक्षक संकुल (उच्च प्रचक्रण संकुल) कहलाते हैं। इसके अतिरिक्त संकुलों की प्रकृति अनुचुम्बकीय अथवा प्रतिचुम्बकीय हो सकती है। इस सिद्धांत की कमियाँ हैं कि इसमें अनेकों कल्पनाएँ सम्मिलित हैं तथा यह संकुल के रंग की व्याख्या नहीं कर पाता है।
questions.text_english: The nature of bonding, structure of the coordination compound can be explained to some extent by valence bond theory. The central metal atom/ion makes available a number of vacant orbitals equal to its coordination number. The appropriate atomic orbitals (s, p and d) of the metal hybridise to give a set of equivalent orbitals of definite geometry such as square planar, tetrahedral, octahedral and so on. A strong covalent bond is formed only when the orbitals overlap to the maximum extent. The d-orbitals involved in the hybridisation may be either inner d-orbitals i.e. (n–1) d or outer d-orbitals i.e. nd. The complexes formed are called inner orbital complex (low spin complex) and outer orbital complex (high spin complex) respectively. Further, the complexes can be paramagnetic or diamagnetic in nature. The drawbacks of this theory are that this involves number of assumptions and also does not explain the colour of the complex.

sub_questions.text: प्रागुक्ति कीजिए कि [CoF₆]³⁻ प्रतिचुम्बकीय है अथवा अनुचुम्बकीय, और क्यों? [परमाणु क्रमांक: Co = 27]
sub_questions.text_english: Predict whether [CoF₆]³⁻ is diamagnetic or paramagnetic and why? [Atomic number: Co = 27]

key_points: Co is +3, electronic config of Co3+ is [Ar]3d6
F- is weak field ligand, so high spin complex: t2g4 eg2 with 4 unpaired electrons
Paramagnetic

sub_questions.solution: [CoF₆]³⁻ is paramagnetic. Co has atomic number 27 and its ground state electronic configuration is [Ar] 3d⁷ 4s². In Co³⁺, two electrons are lost from 4s and one from 3d, giving the configuration [Ar] 3d⁶. Fluoride (F⁻) is a weak field ligand, so it does not cause pairing of electrons. In the octahedral field with weak ligands (Δ₀ < P), the d⁶ configuration in the high spin arrangement is t₂⁴ e², giving 4 unpaired electrons. Because of unpaired electrons, [CoF₆]³⁻ is paramagnetic.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the coordination number of Co in [Co(en)₂ Cl₂]⁺?

key_points: Coordination number is 6
en is bidentate (donates 2 bonds), two en give 4 bonds, two Cl give 2 bonds, total = 6

sub_questions.solution: The coordination number of Co in [Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺ is 6. Ethylenediamine (en) is a bidentate ligand that donates two pairs of electrons (through its two NH₂ groups) to the metal. Two 'en' molecules contribute 4 coordinate bonds, and two Cl⁻ ions each contribute 1 coordinate bond (2 total). The total number of coordinate bonds = 4 + 2 = 6. Hence the coordination number is 6.

'Di' is used as a prefix for two of each. The oxidation state of Pt is calculated: overall charge = +2, two Cl give −2, two NH₃ give 0, so Pt = +4, i.e. platinum(IV). संयोजकता आबंध सिद्धांत के आधार पर [Ni(NH₃)₆]²⁺ की आकृति तथा संकरण का निगमन कीजिए। [परमाणु क्रमांक: Ni = 28]
sub_questions.text_english:
Explain [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is an inner orbital or outer orbital complex.
OR
Using valence bond theory, deduce the shape and hybridisation of [Ni(NH₃)₆]²⁺ [Atomic number of Ni = 28]

key_points: Co3+ has [Ar]3d6; NH3 is strong field ligand so d2sp3 hybridisation (inner orbital)
Uses (n-1)d orbitals = 3d, hence inner orbital complex (low spin)

sub_questions.solution:
[Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is an inner orbital complex (low spin complex). Co³⁺ has the electronic configuration [Ar] 3d⁶. NH₃ is a strong field ligand that causes the pairing of the six d-electrons into three t₂ orbitals (t₂⁶ e⁰), leaving the two e orbitals empty. The two empty 3d (inner d) orbitals, along with one 4s and three 4p orbitals, undergo d²sp³ hybridisation to form six equivalent hybrid orbitals directed towards the corners of a regular octahedron. Since inner d-orbitals [(n–1)d = 3d] are used, it is an inner orbital complex. It has no unpaired electrons and is therefore diamagnetic.

OR: For [Ni(NH₃)₆]²⁺ — Ni (Z=28) has configuration [Ar] 3d⁸ 4s². Ni²⁺ has [Ar] 3d⁸. NH₃ is a moderate to strong field ligand. Two 4p orbitals of Ni²⁺ are empty but the 3d orbitals have 2 unpaired electrons. The hybridisation is sp³d² using outer d-orbitals (4d), making it an outer orbital complex. The shape is octahedral and the complex is paramagnetic due to 2 unpaired electrons.

questions.text: गैल्वेनी सेल में, रेडॉक्स अभिक्रिया की रासायनिक ऊर्जा, विद्युत ऊर्जा में परिवर्तित होती है, जबकि वैद्युतअपघटनी सेल में विद्युत धारा प्रवाहित करने पर रेडॉक्स अभिक्रिया होती है। सरलतम गैल्वेनी सेल में Zn छड़ को ZnSO₄ विलयन में रखा जाता है और Cu छड़ को CuSO₄ विलयन में रखा जाता है। दोनों छड़ों को वोल्टमीटर के माध्यम से धात्विक तार द्वारा जोड़ा जाता है। दोनों विलयनों को लवण सेतु द्वारा जोड़ा जाता है। दोनों इलेक्ट्रोडों के इलेक्ट्रोड विभवों के अंतर को वैद्युत वाहक बल (emf) कहा जाता है। वैद्युतअपघटन प्रक्रम में विद्युत धारा प्रवाहित करने पर पदार्थ का अपघटन होता है। किसी सेल में से एक मोल विद्युत आवेश प्रवाहित करने पर द्विसंयोजक आयन जैसे Cu²⁺ के आधा मोल विसर्जित होते हैं। सर्वप्रथम वैद्युतअपघटनी नियम के रूप में फैराडे ने इसे सूत्रबद्ध किया था।
questions.text_english: In a galvanic cell, chemical energy of a redox reaction is converted into electrical energy, whereas in an electrolytic cell the redox reaction occurs on passing electricity. The simplest galvanic cell is in which Zn rod is placed in a solution of ZnSO₄ and Cu rod is placed in a solution of CuSO₄. The two rods are connected by a metallic wire through a voltmeter. The two solutions are joined by a salt bridge. The difference between the two electrode potentials of the two electrodes is known as electromotive force. In the process of electrolysis, the decomposition of a substance takes place by passing an electric current. One mole of electric charge when passed through a cell will discharge half a mole of a divalent metal ion such as Cu²⁺. This was first formulated by Faraday in the form of laws of electrolysis.

sub_questions.text: गैल्वेनी सेल में लवण सेतु का क्या प्रकार्य है?
sub_questions.text_english: What is the function of a salt bridge in a galvanic cell?

key_points: Maintains electrical neutrality by allowing ions to flow between two half cells
Prevents mixing of solutions while allowing ionic conduction

sub_questions.solution: The salt bridge serves two functions in a galvanic cell: (1) It maintains electrical neutrality in both the half-cells by allowing ions (cations towards the cathode compartment and anions towards the anode compartment) to migrate and balance the charge build-up. (2) It completes the electric circuit by providing a path for ionic conduction between the two half-cells while preventing the direct mixing of the two solutions.

sub_questions.text: गैल्वेनी सेल कब एक वैद्युतअपघटनी सेल की भाँति व्यवहार करता है?
sub_questions.text_english: When does galvanic cell behave like an electrolytic cell?

key_points: When external opposing potential greater than EMF of the cell is applied
Reaction is reversed and cell acts as electrolytic cell

sub_questions.solution: A galvanic cell behaves like an electrolytic cell when an external opposing potential greater than the EMF of the cell is applied to it. Under these conditions, the cell reaction is reversed — instead of generating electricity, the cell consumes electrical energy to drive a non-spontaneous redox reaction. The electrode that was the anode in the galvanic cell becomes the cathode, and vice versa.

क्या जिंक से बने बर्तन में कॉपर सल्फेट विलयन भंडारित किया जा सकता है? E° सेल के मान की सहायता से व्याख्या कीजिए। (E° Cu²⁺/Cu = 0.34 V) (E° Zn²⁺/Zn = –0.76 V)
अथवा
निम्नलिखित के अपचयन के लिए कितने फैराडे आवेश की आवश्यकता होगी?
(i) 1 मोल MnO₄⁻ को Mn²⁺ में
(ii) 1 मोल H₂O को O₂ में
sub_questions.text_english:
Can copper sulphate solution be stored in a pot made of zinc? Explain with the help of the value of E° cell. (E° Cu²⁺/Cu = 0.34 V) (E° Zn²⁺/Zn = –0.76 V)
OR
How much charge in terms of Faraday is required for the following:
(i) 1 mol of MnO₄⁻ to Mn²⁺
(ii) 1 mol of H₂O to O₂

key_points: No, copper sulphate cannot be stored in zinc pot
E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = 0.34-(-0.76) = 1.10 V (positive), so reaction is spontaneous
Zn will displace Cu from CuSO4, dissolving the pot

sub_questions.solution:
No, copper sulphate solution cannot be stored in a pot made of zinc. The cell reaction would be: Zn (anode) → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻ and Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu (cathode). E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = 0.34 – (–0.76) = +1.10 V. Since E°cell is positive, the reaction is spontaneous. Zinc is a stronger reducing agent than copper, so zinc will displace copper from the copper sulphate solution and the zinc pot will gradually dissolve, making it unsuitable for storage.

OR:
(i) MnO₄⁻ → Mn²⁺: Manganese changes from +7 to +2, a gain of 5 electrons. So 1 mol MnO₄⁻ requires 5 Faradays.
(ii) H₂O → O₂: Oxygen in water is –2 and in O₂ is 0, so each oxygen loses 2 electrons. One mole of H₂O has one mole of oxygen atoms. But the reaction 2H₂O → O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ shows 4 electrons transferred per O₂ molecule from 2 H₂O. For 1 mol H₂O, charge = 2 Faradays.

sub_questions.text: जिंक को संक्रमण तत्व क्यों नहीं माना जाता है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why Zinc is not regarded as a transition element?

key_points: Zinc has completely filled d-orbitals in ground state and in all its oxidation states
Transition elements must have partially filled d-orbitals in at least one oxidation state

sub_questions.solution: Zinc (Zn, Z = 30) is not regarded as a transition element because its d-orbitals are completely filled (3d¹⁰) both in its ground state ([Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s²) and in its only stable oxidation state Zn²⁺ ([Ar] 3d¹⁰). A transition element is defined as one which has partially filled d-orbitals in its ground state or in any of its commonly occurring oxidation states. Since zinc does not satisfy this condition, it is not classified as a transition element.

sub_questions.text: लैन्थेनॉयड आकुंचन क्या है?
sub_questions.text_english: What is Lanthanoid contraction?

key_points: Progressive decrease in atomic and ionic radii of lanthanoids from La to Lu
Due to poor shielding by 4f electrons

sub_questions.solution: Lanthanoid contraction refers to the steady and regular decrease in the atomic and ionic radii of the lanthanoid elements with increasing atomic number, from lanthanum (La) to lutetium (Lu). This contraction occurs because as protons are added to the nucleus, the 4f electrons that are also being added provide poor shielding of the nuclear charge from each other due to the diffuse nature of f-orbitals. Consequently, the effective nuclear charge experienced by outer electrons increases progressively, pulling them closer to the nucleus and decreasing the size.

sub_questions.text: जिंक की तुलना में क्रोमियम की प्रथम आयनन एन्थैल्पी निम्नतर क्यों होती है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is first ionization enthalpy of chromium lower than that of Zn?

key_points: Zn has completely filled 3d and 4s2 configuration, more stable
Cr has 3d5 4s1 half-filled configuration which is stable but 4s1 electron is easier to remove than removing from full 4s2

sub_questions.solution: The first ionisation enthalpy of chromium (Cr) is lower than that of zinc (Zn). Zinc has the electronic configuration [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s²; both its 3d and 4s orbitals are completely filled, giving it extra stability. Chromium has the configuration [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹; it has only one electron in the 4s orbital. Although the half-filled 3d⁵ configuration provides extra stability to Cr, the single 4s electron in chromium is more easily removed (lower ionisation enthalpy) compared to removing one of the paired 4s electrons in zinc, which requires overcoming additional electron–electron repulsion. Hence, Cr has a lower first ionisation enthalpy than Zn.

sub_questions.text: संक्रमण तत्व क्यों उत्तम उत्प्रेरक होते हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: Why are transition elements good catalysts?

key_points: Ability to exhibit variable oxidation states
Large surface area and ability to adsorb reactants on surface
Ability to form intermediate compounds with reactants

sub_questions.solution: Transition elements are good catalysts due to two main reasons. First, they can exhibit multiple (variable) oxidation states, which allows them to form intermediate compounds with reactants by changing their oxidation state temporarily, and then revert to the original state after the reaction — effectively providing a lower energy pathway. Second, transition metals and their compounds have large surface areas and can adsorb reactant molecules on their surfaces, bringing them into close proximity and facilitating reaction. For example, iron acts as a catalyst in the Haber process and vanadium pentoxide in the Contact process.

sub_questions.text: संक्रमण धातुओं के यौगिक सामान्यत: रंगीन होते हैं। कारण दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Compounds of transition metals are generally coloured. Give reason.

key_points: Transition metal compounds have partially filled d-orbitals
d-d transitions absorb certain wavelengths of visible light
Complementary colour is observed

sub_questions.solution: Compounds of transition metals are generally coloured because they have partially filled d-orbitals. When visible light falls on a transition metal compound, electrons in the lower energy d-orbitals absorb energy (photons of specific wavelengths) and are excited to higher energy d-orbitals (d–d transitions). The wavelength of light absorbed corresponds to the energy gap between the split d-orbitals, which lies in the visible range. The complementary colour of the absorbed wavelength is transmitted, giving the compound its characteristic colour. Compounds where d-orbitals are empty (Sc³⁺: d⁰) or completely filled (Zn²⁺: d¹⁰) are colourless.

sub_questions.text: KMnO₄ एवं K₂MnO₄ की तुलना में, कौन सा एक अनुचुम्बकीय है, और क्यों?
sub_questions.text_english: Out of KMnO₄ and K₂MnO₄, which one is paramagnetic and why?

key_points: K2MnO4 is paramagnetic
In K2MnO4, Mn is +6 (d1 configuration) with one unpaired electron
In KMnO4, Mn is +7 (d0 configuration) with no unpaired electrons, so diamagnetic

sub_questions.solution: K₂MnO₄ (potassium manganate) is paramagnetic, while KMnO₄ (potassium permanganate) is diamagnetic. In KMnO₄, the oxidation state of Mn is +7, giving it a 3d⁰ configuration with no unpaired electrons — hence it is diamagnetic. In K₂MnO₄, the oxidation state of Mn is +6, giving it a 3d¹ configuration with one unpaired electron — hence it is paramagnetic. The presence of unpaired electrons is responsible for paramagnetism.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित आयनिक समीकरण पूर्ण कीजिए: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ →
sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following ionic equation: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14 H⁺ + 6e⁻ →
sub_questions.solution: The complete ionic equation is: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O. In dichromate ion, chromium is in the +6 oxidation state. Upon reduction, each Cr⁶⁺ gains 3 electrons to become Cr³⁺. Two chromium atoms gain a total of 6 electrons, which matches the 6e⁻ on the left. The 14 H⁺ ions combine with the 7 oxygen atoms from Cr₂O₇²⁻ to form 7 H₂O molecules, balancing the equation.

sub_questions.text: प्रतिलोम परासरण को परिभाषित कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Define reverse osmosis.

key_points: Application of pressure greater than osmotic pressure on solution side
Solvent molecules pass from solution to pure solvent through semipermeable membrane

sub_questions.solution: Reverse osmosis is the process in which the flow of solvent molecules is reversed by applying an external pressure greater than the osmotic pressure of the solution. When excess pressure is applied on the solution side, solvent molecules are forced to pass from the more concentrated solution to the pure solvent side through a semipermeable membrane, which is opposite to the direction of normal osmosis. This process is used in the desalination of sea water.

sub_questions.text: जलीय स्पीशीज़ के लिए गर्म जल की तुलना में ठंडे जल में रहना अधिक आरामदायक क्यों है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why are aquatic species more comfortable in cold water in comparison to warm water?

key_points: Solubility of oxygen is higher in cold water than warm water
Cold water contains more dissolved oxygen for aquatic life to breathe

sub_questions.solution: Aquatic species are more comfortable in cold water because the solubility of oxygen (and other gases) in water is higher at lower temperatures. According to Henry's law, the solubility of a gas decreases as temperature increases. Cold water therefore contains a higher concentration of dissolved oxygen, which is essential for the respiration of fish and other aquatic organisms. In warm water, the reduced oxygen content makes it difficult for aquatic species to breathe, causing discomfort or even death.

sub_questions.text: 303 K पर 100 g जल में 2 g ग्लूकोस (M = 180 g mol⁻¹) को घोलकर विलयन बनाया गया। शुद्ध जल का वाष्प दाब 32.8 mm Hg है। विलयन का वाष्प दाब क्या होगा?
sub_questions.text_english: A solution containing 2 g of glucose (M = 180 g mol⁻¹) in 100 g of water is prepared at 303 K. If the vapour pressure of pure water at 303 K is 32.8 mm Hg, what would be the vapour pressure of the solution?

key_points: Moles of glucose = 2/180 = 0.0111 mol
Moles of water = 100/18 = 5.556 mol
P_solution = P0 x mole fraction of solvent = 32.8 x (1-0.001993) = 32.734 mm Hg

sub_questions.solution: Moles of glucose = 2/180 = 0.01111 mol. Moles of water = 100/18 = 5.556 mol. Mole fraction of water (solvent) = 5.556/(5.556 + 0.01111) = 5.556/5.5671 = 0.998. By Raoult's law: Pₛₒₗᵤₜᵢₒₙ = P₀ × xₛₒₗᵥᵉₙₜ = 32.8 × 0.998 = 32.734 mm Hg. Alternatively, using the lowering formula: ΔP/P₀ = mole fraction of solute = 0.01111/5.5671 = 0.001996. ΔP = 32.8 × 0.001996 = 0.0655 mm Hg. Pₛₒₗᵤₜᵢₒₙ = 32.8 – 0.0655 ≈ 32.73 mm Hg.

sub_questions.text: एथेनोइक अम्ल को बेन्जीन में घोलने पर वान्ट हॉफ गुणक एक से कम होगा या अधिक?
sub_questions.text_english: Predict whether Van't Hoff factor will be less or greater than one, when Ethanoic acid is dissolved in benzene.

key_points: Van't Hoff factor (i) will be less than 1
Ethanoic acid dimerises in benzene through hydrogen bonding, reducing the number of solute particles

sub_questions.solution: When ethanoic acid (acetic acid) is dissolved in benzene, the Van't Hoff factor (i) will be less than 1. Ethanoic acid undergoes dimerisation in benzene through intermolecular hydrogen bonding between the carboxyl groups of two molecules, forming a cyclic dimer. This reduces the actual number of solute particles in solution compared to what would be expected if no association occurred. Since i = actual number of particles / expected number of particles, and the actual number is less than expected, i < 1.

sub_questions.text: आदर्श विलयन की परिभाषा लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Define ideal solution.

key_points: Solution that obeys Raoult's law over all concentrations and temperatures
No change in volume or enthalpy on mixing

sub_questions.solution: An ideal solution is one that obeys Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration at all temperatures. In an ideal solution, the intermolecular interactions between solute–solvent molecules are exactly equal in strength to those between solute–solute and solvent–solvent molecules. As a result, there is no change in enthalpy (ΔHₘᵢₓ = 0) and no change in volume (ΔVₘᵢₓ = 0) upon mixing. Dilute solutions of non-electrolytes, such as benzene–toluene mixtures, approximately behave as ideal solutions.

sub_questions.text: CaCl₂ (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 111 g mol⁻¹) के उस द्रव्यमान का परिकलन कीजिए जिसे 500 g जल में विलीन करने पर हिमांक में 2K की कमी हो जाए। (Kₑ = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹)
sub_questions.text_english: Calculate the mass of CaCl₂ (molar mass = 111 g mol⁻¹) to be dissolved in 500 g of water to lower its freezing point by 2K, assuming CaCl₂ undergoes complete dissociation. (Kₑ = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹)

key_points: CaCl2 dissociates into 3 ions, so i=3
Delta Tf = i x Kf x m => 2 = 3 x 1.86 x m => m = 0.3584 mol/kg
Moles of CaCl2 = 0.3584 x 0.5 = 0.1792 mol

sub_questions.solution: CaCl₂ dissociates completely as: CaCl₂ → Ca²⁺ + 2Cl⁻, giving 3 ions per formula unit. So the Van't Hoff factor i = 3. Using the formula ΔT = i × K × m: 2 = 3 × 1.86 × m. Molality m = 2/(3 × 1.86) = 2/5.58 = 0.3584 mol kg⁻¹. Mass of solvent = 500 g = 0.5 kg. Moles of CaCl₂ = 0.3584 × 0.5 = 0.1792 mol. Mass of CaCl₂ = 0.1792 × 111 = 19.89 ≈ 19.9 g. Therefore, approximately 19.9 g of CaCl₂ must be dissolved.

(a) An amide 'A' with molecular formula C₇H₇ON undergoes Hoffmann Bromamide degradation reaction to give amine 'B'. B on treatment with nitrous acid at 273-278 K form 'C' and on treatment with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide forms 'D'. 'C' on treatment, with ethanol gives 'E'. Identify 'A', 'B', 'C' 'D' and 'E.' and write the sequence of chemical equations.
OR

(i)
(1) What is Hinsberg's reagent?

C₂H₅NH₂, (C₂H₅)₃ N, (C₂H₅)₂ NH
(ii) Give reasons for the following:

sub_questions.text: C₇H₇ON आण्विक सूत्र का एमाइड 'A' से A, B, C, D, E की पहचान और रासायनिक समीकरण।
sub_questions.text_english: Identify A, B, C, D, E and write the sequence of chemical equations for the amide 'A' with molecular formula C7H7ON.

key_points: A = benzamide (C6H5CONH2, mol formula C7H7ON)
B = aniline (C6H5NH2) via Hoffmann bromamide degradation
C = benzene diazonium chloride (C6H5N2+Cl-) via reaction with HNO2/HCl at 273-278K
D = phenyl isocyanide (C6H5NC) via carbylamine reaction (CHCl3 + alc. KOH)
E = ethyl benzoate (C6H5COOC2H5) from diazonium salt + ethanol? Actually C from diazonium reacts with ethanol... correction: C reacts with ethanol to give phenol/ethyl ester

sub_questions.solution: A is benzamide (C₆H₅CONH₂, molecular formula C₇H₇ON). Step 1 (Hoffmann Bromamide degradation): C₆H₅CONH₂ + Br₂ + 4KOH → C₆H₅NH₂ (B = aniline) + K₂CO₃ + 2KBr + 2H₂O. Benzamide loses one carbon as CO₂, giving aniline. Step 2 (Diazotisation at 273–278 K): C₆H₅NH₂ + NaNO₂ + HCl → C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻ (C = benzene diazonium chloride) + NaCl + 2H₂O. Step 3 (Carbylamine reaction with CHCl₃ and alc. KOH): C₆H₅NH₂ + CHCl₃ + 3KOH(alc.) → C₆H₅NC (D = phenyl isocyanide/isonitrile) + 3KCl + 3H₂O. Step 4 (Reaction of diazonium salt C with ethanol): C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻ + C₂H₅OH → C₆H₅OC₂H₅ (E = phenetole/ethoxybenzene) + N₂ + HCl. Thus A = Benzamide, B = Aniline, C = Benzene diazonium chloride, D = Phenyl isocyanide, E = Phenetole (ethoxybenzene).

sub_questions.text: हिन्सबर्ग अभिकर्मक क्या है?
sub_questions.text_english: What is Hinsberg's reagent?

key_points: Hinsberg's reagent is benzenesulphonyl chloride (C6H5SO2Cl)

sub_questions.solution: Hinsberg's reagent is benzenesulphonyl chloride (C₆H₅SO₂Cl). It is used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary amines. Primary amines react with it to form a sulphonamide that is soluble in NaOH (due to an acidic N–H). Secondary amines form a sulphonamide insoluble in NaOH. Tertiary amines do not react with Hinsberg's reagent.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित यौगिकों को गैस प्रावस्था में उनकी बढ़ती हुई क्षारकीय सामर्थ्य में व्यवस्थित कीजिए: C₂H₅NH₂, (C₂H₅)₃ N, (C₂H₅)₂ NH
sub_questions.text_english: Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of their basic strength in gaseous phase: C₂H₅NH₂, (C₂H₅)₃ N, (C₂H₅)₂ NH

key_points: In gaseous phase, basic strength order: C2H5NH2 < (C2H5)2NH < (C2H5)3N
More alkyl groups = more electron donation = greater electron density on N = stronger base in gas phase

sub_questions.solution: In the gaseous phase, the basic strength of amines increases with the number of electron-donating alkyl groups attached to nitrogen, because solvation effects (which reduce the order in aqueous solution) are absent. Therefore, the order of increasing basic strength in gaseous phase is: C₂H₅NH₂ (primary) < (C₂H₅)₂NH (secondary) < (C₂H₅)₃N (tertiary). Triethylamine has three ethyl groups donating electrons to nitrogen, making it the strongest base in gas phase.

sub_questions.text: ऐनिलीन की तुलना में मेथिल ऐमीन अधिक क्षारकीय है। कारण दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Methyl amine is more basic than aniline. Give reason.

key_points: In aniline, lone pair of N is delocalised into benzene ring by resonance
Electron density on N decreases, making aniline a weaker base than methylamine

sub_questions.solution: Methylamine (CH₃NH₂) is more basic than aniline (C₆H₅NH₂) because in aniline, the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom is delocalised into the benzene ring through resonance (conjugation with the π system of the ring). This decreases the electron density on nitrogen, making it less available to donate a proton and thus less basic. In methylamine, the methyl group donates electrons to nitrogen by the inductive effect, increasing electron density on nitrogen and making it a stronger base.

sub_questions.text: ऐनिलीन, ब्रोमीन जल के साथ शीघ्रता से अभिक्रिया करके 2, 4, 6-ट्राइब्रोमो ऐनिलीन देती है। कारण दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Aniline readily reacts with bromine water to give 2, 4, 6-tribromoaniline. Give reason.

key_points: -NH2 group is strongly activating and ortho/para directing
High electron density at ortho and para positions allows easy electrophilic bromination without catalyst

sub_questions.solution: Aniline readily reacts with bromine water to give 2,4,6-tribromoaniline because the –NH₂ group is a powerful electron-donating group that activates the benzene ring towards electrophilic aromatic substitution. The lone pair of electrons on nitrogen delocalises into the ring, greatly increasing electron density at the ortho and para positions. This makes aniline so reactive that it reacts with bromine water (without any catalyst) in all three positions (2, 4, and 6) simultaneously to give the trisubstituted product. The reaction is instantaneous and does not require a Lewis acid catalyst.

sub_questions.text: तृतीयक ऐमीनो की तुलना में प्राथमिक ऐमीनो के क्वथनांक उच्चतर होते हैं। कारण दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Primary amines have higher boiling points than tertiary amines. Give reason.

key_points: Primary amines can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds through N-H...N interactions
Tertiary amines have no N-H bond so cannot form hydrogen bonds among themselves

sub_questions.solution: Primary amines have higher boiling points than tertiary amines of comparable molecular mass because primary amines can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds through their N–H bonds (both as hydrogen bond donors and acceptors). These additional intermolecular attractive forces require more energy (higher temperature) to overcome, resulting in higher boiling points. Tertiary amines have no N–H bond; they cannot form hydrogen bonds among themselves. They only experience van der Waals forces, which are weaker, so they have lower boiling points.
